solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reads list for new naval officer

indicators.note: something new is made over, so these three words are formed afresh into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a list to welcome a newly arrived officer aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the officer, but it tells you to rearrange READS LIST FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Sea Lord is the professional head of Britain's Royal Navy, its most senior serving officer.

clue.text: Gin drunk inside taverns for a spell

indicators.note: the anagram goes inside the word for taverns

parts.note: inns are taverns or pubs

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of gin are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spends a period drinking gin in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the drinker but signals the anagram; 'a spell' is not magic but a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is a spell or period of activity, from cricket, where it is a batting turn.

clue.text: Tight-lipped, overhaul intelligence agency

parts.note: someone tight-lipped keeps things secret
to service a car or machine is to overhaul it

explanation.surface: A discreet spy agency is undergoing a reorganisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The secret service is a government body gathering intelligence, the British one being MI6.

clue.text: Back runner-up

definitions.meaning: to back a proposal is to support it formally in a meeting
the runner-up finishes just behind the winner

explanation.definitionFit: Supporting a motion and finishing in place two are both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Landmark building's charm — a yard lit subtly

indicators.note: subtly suggests the letters are rearranged in an understated, cunning way

explanation.surface: Praise for a famous building's charm, its courtyard gently illuminated.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiralty Arch is a large ceremonial arch building near Trafalgar Square in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiralty Arch is a famous London landmark at the end of The Mall.

clue.text: Outstanding old annexe

parts.note: a wing is an extension or annexe of a building

explanation.surface: Praise for a superb historic extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means excellent on the surface, but here it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is owing is still unpaid, which is outstanding.

clue.text: Expected around noon, daughter in New Zealand city

indicators.note: the word for expected goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: something due is expected

explanation.surface: A traveller's arrival time: due about midday, with a daughter, in a New Zealand city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city on New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Mate after ring and gemstone

indicators.note: in a down answer, the word for mate coming after the ring places it below

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
pal and mate both mean a friend

explanation.surface: A spouse in search of a ring and a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' suggests a spouse but just means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone known for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: Great alarm in ship: an iceberg!

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit in the run of words that follows, spanning ship, an and iceberg

explanation.surface: A lookout's cry of terror as a vessel heads towards an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's alarm and the definition coincide, which hides the mechanism in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, which is great alarm in other words.

clue.text: Bloomer affected one performing

parts.note: camp means exaggerated and affected in manner
I is the Roman numeral one
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: A clumsy blunder made by a pretentious performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a gaffe but here means a flowering plant, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The campion is a wild flower, and any flowering plant can be called a bloomer in crosswords.

clue.text: Light tail of teal, an aquatic bird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, taken here from teal

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A description of a teal's tail and a water bird, as if in a field guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, so a source of light.

clue.text: Tackle papers, stiff

parts.note: rig means equipment or tackle, as on a boat or for fishing
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Fishing gear and documents that have become stiff and unbending.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid and stiff are synonyms, both meaning unable to bend.

clue.text: A sign, primarily, is put in street to help

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of sign is used
the word is is placed inside the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Instructions for erecting a road sign to guide people.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give help or aid, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Aim at office worker on short time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A goal set for an office worker on reduced hours.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt and an aim are both a try at achieving something.

clue.text: Hit hard with a new advertising phrase

parts.note: to slog is to hit a ball hard and wildly, as in cricket

explanation.surface: An advertising campaign that lands a heavy blow with a fresh catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short catchy phrase used in advertising or campaigning.

clue.text: Good to pay attention, then shine

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention to what is said

explanation.surface: Advice to a pupil: listen well, then you will excel.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or shine with reflected light.

clue.text: Poor-quality rum imbibed by cast

indicators.note: imbibed by means taken inside, so the strange word goes inside the throw word

parts.note: a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Cheap rum drunk by the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' and 'imbibed' suggest drinking, but rum means odd and cast means a throw, SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are badly made and of poor quality.

clue.text: Tories' leader, at heart of crushing defeat, returned in coach

indicators.note: returned means the whole construction is read backwards
the letter goes into the middle of the word for a crushing defeat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Tories'

explanation.surface: A political report: the Conservative leader, central to an election disaster, comes back by coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses ROTUT, which is T placed at the heart of ROUT; 'coach' suggests a bus but means a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor coaches or teaches a pupil privately, so coach is a synonym.

clue.text: Not relaxed in past, perhaps

definitions.meaning: someone who is not relaxed is nervous and strained
the past is one grammatical form of a verb, as are present and future

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both nervous and strained, and a grammatical time form of a verb, of which the past is one example.

clue.text: Crazy heir, way out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of heir and way are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks an heir's chosen path is mad and well off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire means behaving erratically or out of control, close to crazy.

clue.text: Sensitive over a winged nude statue?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: a sore spot is sensitive to touch

explanation.surface: Someone who is touchy about a statue of a naked winged figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue in London's Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piccadilly Circus statue known by this Greek god's name is a winged nude figure.

clue.text: People generally warm on island in the British Isles

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea, part of the British Isles
kind and warm both describe a friendly, caring nature

explanation.surface: A claim that islanders in Britain and Ireland are, on the whole, warm-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, between England and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mankind means the human race, people taken as a whole.

clue.text: Allowance reduced in proportion

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance, as of food

explanation.surface: An allowance cut back proportionately.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a proportion, the relation of one quantity to another.

clue.text: Empty trash, the lot — exactly what's needed

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters of trash

parts.note: the lot is an informal way of saying everything

explanation.surface: A command to throw out all the rubbish at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like a verb about the bin, but it means remove the middle of trash, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: The very thing is an idiom for something perfectly suited to the purpose.
